source: Coil & Shwartz (2023) From chocolate bunny to chocolate crocodile: Do language models understand noun compounds?
finding: Text-davinci-002 with a few-shot prompt paraphrased noun compounds (NCI) almost perfectly once the SemEval 2013 data and scoring were cleaned up.
numbers: Revised SemEval 2013 test set: GPT-3 BERTScore 91.94, ROUGE-L 47.31, METEOR 56.27; over 95% of its paraphrases judged acceptable by a majority of MTurk raters.
limits: Compounds are mostly lexicalised and frequent in web text; automatic metrics disagreed with humans. Only one model family tested.
agent_relevance: Interpretation of familiar compounds is a solved slot for a model. Do not spend scaffold budget on it.

source: Coil & Shwartz (2023) From chocolate bunny to chocolate crocodile: Do language models understand noun compounds?
finding: On conceptualisation of novel compounds (NCC, e.g. chocolate crocodile) GPT-3 beat human writers.
numbers: NCC test set of 105 rare/novel compounds; human-evaluated accuracy: GPT-3 83.81% vs human reference 73.33%.
limits: Humans wrote one paraphrase with no incentive; authors say pay might raise human accuracy. Compounds chosen by low C4 frequency, but GPT-3 trained on newer data.
agent_relevance: A model can be used as the combiner for odd noun pairs. Humans are not the ceiling here.

source: Coil & Shwartz (2023) From chocolate bunny to chocolate crocodile: Do language models understand noun compounds?
finding: GPT-3 accuracy fell on the rarest compounds and its paraphrases often copy web n-grams.
numbers: Share of generated n-grams found in Common Crawl: 34-94% depending on n-gram size; about 97% of copied n-grams for NCI vs 80% for NCC. Accuracy fell as compound corpus frequency fell.
limits: No access to GPT-3 training data; C4 used as proxy.
agent_relevance: Fluent combination of known pairs is partly recall. For distant seed pairs recall will not help, so expect lower quality.

source: Coil & Shwartz (2023) From chocolate bunny to chocolate crocodile: Do language models understand noun compounds?
finding: Typical failure: GPT-3 swapped head and modifier, e.g. defined banana table as a banana rather than a table.
numbers: Anecdotal examples in error analysis; no rate reported for this error alone.
quote: GPT-3 defines a banana table as a banana rather than a table
limits: Head-modifier asymmetry is a core human principle (Wisniewski); the model sometimes breaks it.
agent_relevance: Add a code check that the output is an instance of the head noun (endocentric test).

source: Li, Carlson & Potts (2022) Systematicity in GPT-3's interpretation of novel English noun compounds
finding: Experiment 1: GPT-3 free definitions of 38 novel artifact/natural-kind compounds matched the relation mix humans gave in Levin et al. (2019).
numbers: 456 generations (38 compounds x 3 prompt types x 4 temperatures); Pearson r between GPT-3 and human meta-relation distributions all high, best 0.93 (few-shot prompt, T=0.7). Annotator Fleiss kappa 0.844 (meta-relations), 0.767 (subtypes).
limits: Match could come from lexical item knowledge, not concept-type reasoning (authors' own caveat).
agent_relevance: Surface agreement with human combination patterns is cheap; it is not proof of concept-level reasoning.

source: Li, Carlson & Potts (2022) Systematicity in GPT-3's interpretation of novel English noun compounds
finding: Experiments 2-3: with nonsense words standing in for real nouns, GPT-3 did not show the artifact vs natural-kind effect, and the match to humans collapsed.
numbers: Pearson correlation with the original human distribution fell to 0.105 (vs 0.93 in Exp 1). Exclusion (unusable output) rates were much higher; about 30% of exclusions were head/modifier inversions.
limits: Exclusion table values garbled in text extraction; only the 0.105, 0.93 and 30% figures were checked.
agent_relevance: Test the agent on controls where lexical shortcuts are removed. A pass on real words may be memory.

source: Rambelli, Chersoni, Collacciani & Bolognesi (2024) Can LLMs interpret noun-noun compounds? Lexicalized and novel compounds
finding: Open 7B models (Llama-2, Falcon, Mistral; base and instruct) picked the right relation paraphrase for lexicalised compounds only 38-45% of the time by surprisal.
numbers: Surprisal accuracy on LNC (lexicalised): BERT-large 26.2%, GPT2-xl 33.8%; instruct Llama-2 44.8%, Mistral 42.2%, Falcon 38.0%. 200 compounds were right for all three models. Multiple-choice prompting on Nakov data: Llama-2 / Mistral 63.2-64.8%.
limits: Small open models only; 9-way paraphrase choice is harder than free paraphrase. Instruction tuning did not reliably help (Falcon instruct worse than base).
agent_relevance: Choosing among relation labels is a weak area for small models. Free paraphrase then check is more reliable than a forced relation menu.

source: Rambelli, Chersoni, Collacciani & Bolognesi (2024) Can LLMs interpret noun-noun compounds? Lexicalized and novel compounds
finding: Accuracy rose with concreteness and varied strongly by relation class.
numbers: Concreteness regression coefficient 0.703 (SE 0.133, p<0.001). Per-class accuracy 80-94% for FROM, CAUSE2, MAKE2; production-type about 96% vs its reversed class about 15%. Mistral reached 59% in 1-shot on Nakov.
limits: Class sizes small for some relations (one class only 5 compounds).
agent_relevance: Abstract-noun pairs (likely distant-domain seeds) will be interpreted worse than concrete pairs. Prefer concrete seeds or add grounding.

source: Rambelli, Chersoni, Collacciani & Bolognesi (2024) Can LLMs interpret noun-noun compounds? Lexicalized and novel compounds
finding: Novel-compound test: replace head or modifier of a known compound with a hypernym. Models transfer the known relation poorly, and changing the head hurts more than changing the modifier.
numbers: Mistral-7B-Instruct prompt accuracy on NNC: sameHead 0.578 (1-shot) / 0.531 (3-shot); sameModifier 0.469 / 0.30. Llama-2 and Falcon 0.047-0.219. Example CONTAINMENT-R 1-shot .474 vs .37, 3-shot .737 vs .05 (novel modifier vs novel head; assignment inferred from text).
limits: More shots hurt for sameModifier (0.469 to 0.30): prompt examples can bias models. Hypernym replacement may create odd compounds.
agent_relevance: More few-shot examples can reduce quality on novel pairs; test shot count, do not assume more is better.

source: Rodriguez, Wang & Pylkkanen (2024) Do neural language models compose concepts the way humans can?
finding: Adjective-noun composition by inference (not syntax): 8 older neural LMs diverged from humans. Only GPT-2 came close overall; RoBERTa did well only on local composition.
numbers: Humans 94.3% overall (40 Prolific raters, 100 sentence pairs). GPT-2 71.75%, BERT-large 58.5%, RoBERTa 58.0%, GPT 48.25%, BERT 43.75%, DistilBERT 34.75%, XLNet 26.75%, GPT-2-large 22.0%. Non-local adjective: humans 89.8% vs RoBERTa 19.3%.
limits: Adjective-noun not noun-noun; models are 2018-2020 era, not modern LLMs. Binary surprisal contrast only.
agent_relevance: Inference-based combination (modifier info arriving from a distant clause) is much weaker than adjacency. Put the two seed concepts adjacent in the prompt.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans (KOMBINE)
finding: KOMBINE gives 35 LLMs random distant entity pairs (blue whale + mattress) and asks for association, analogy and blending. Blending is hardest for models.
numbers: Mean valid rates across 35 LLMs: association 59.0%, analogy 53.4%, blend 43.4% (valid generic space found). Models 10-16 points better at association and analogy than at blends. LLM judge panel agrees with humans 75% on unanimous items.
limits: LLM-judge scoring; sampled at T=0.9; results are the paper's own.
agent_relevance: Direct test of distant-seed combination. Expect fewer than half of forced blends to be valid, so a code gate is needed.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans (KOMBINE)
finding: Abstraction bottleneck: models fail to find the shared abstraction between the two inputs, but once found, the blended concept is coherent.
numbers: Valid generic space found only 43.4% on average; conditioned on that, coherent blend described 97.1% of the time.
limits: Judge-based labels.
agent_relevance: Insert an explicit 'find the shared abstraction' step that code checks, before asking for the blend.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans (KOMBINE)
finding: Inventive homogeneity: different models invent the same properties for the same seed pair.
numbers: 19.9% (412/2,070) of invented concepts reuse 2+ properties invented by another model; same-provider models 2.3x more likely to reuse than cross-provider; reuse 14x more likely on blends than analogies (37.3% vs 2.6%).
limits: Embedding-threshold match on property pairs.
agent_relevance: Backs guardrail G4: samples from one model are not independent. Diversity must come from the seeds, not from resampling.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans (KOMBINE)
finding: Humans (75 Prolific adults) scored below nearly every LLM on all three tasks; both struggle most on blending; they use different regions of semantic space.
numbers: Human vs LLM valid rate: association 22.1% vs 59.0%; analogy 32.9% vs 53.4%; blend 12.8% vs 43.4%. Humans find analogy easier than association; LLMs the reverse.
limits: Difference driven mainly by validity (utility), not novelty; crowd workers on a hard task.
agent_relevance: Human-model complementarity: seeds from a human or another model's distribution add diversity the model alone lacks.

source: Wang, Petridis, Kwon, Ma & Chilton (2023) PopBlends: strategies for conceptual blending with LLMs
finding: PopBlends is a pipeline of fixed steps: expand each concept with associations (GPT-3 plus knowledge base), find connecting concepts, then search scenes. The model fills slots, code ranks. This is a conceptual-combination method already built as a loop.
numbers: Stage-1 accuracy of connecting concepts: 56.0% (No-GPT), 55.3% (Half-GPT), 58.7% (Full-GPT); at least 1 of 5 correct: 90.0%, 96.6%, 93.3%. Pairs with at least one good connection across strategies: 93.3%.
limits: Stage-1 labels by annotators; GPT-3 sometimes hallucinated a link not in the source domain.
agent_relevance: Closest existing design to our open mode: expand, connect, check, generate several, filter by code. Per-item hit rate about 56% means generate five and filter.

source: Wang, Petridis, Kwon, Ma & Chilton (2023) PopBlends: strategies for conceptual blending with LLMs
finding: Within-subject user study: the tool doubled the number of blend ideas and about halved mental load versus brainstorming plus web search.
numbers: N=10 students, 6 pop culture-product pairs, 5 min each. Ideas per pair 2.03 (SD 0.84) vs 0.87 (SD 0.56), paired Wilcoxon p<0.001. NASA-TLX mental demand 2.85 (SD 1.08) vs 5.80 (SD 2.14), p=0.004. All 10 preferred it.
limits: Small sample, amateur designers, no quality rating of final blends.
agent_relevance: Scaffolded association expansion helps people on distant pairs; a similar loop may help a model.

source: Ge & Parikh (2021) Visual conceptual blending with large-scale language and vision models
finding: Language models beat a ConceptNet knowledge base at proposing the shared property a blend hinges on (simile data, e.g. moon + orange via 'sliced').
numbers: 66,442 property-object pairs; 1,000 candidates each. ConceptNet P@1000 about 5.9 vs best language model 66.38; P@100 2.70 vs 24.84. Larger LMs better. 96.34% of objects found in ConceptNet. Table layout garbled; row labels inferred from order.
limits: Simile dataset, not noun-noun compounds; 2021 models.
agent_relevance: LM is a better source of cross-concept bridging properties than a symbolic KB, but P@10 stays very low.

source: Ge & Parikh (2021) Visual conceptual blending with large-scale language and vision models
finding: Pipeline: pick related object, pick shared property, write one-sentence blend, then render. Humans judged blends on unpacking, integration and quality.
numbers: 20 blend descriptions (half model-generated, half hand-written); AMT pairwise preference on 6 questions: large text-to-image models beat a DF-GAN baseline significantly.
limits: Only 20 descriptions; preference test, no absolute scores.
agent_relevance: Fauconnier-Turner principles (unpacking, integration) can be turned into check questions.

source: Vemuri, Shah & Varma (2024) How well do deep learning models capture human concepts? The typicality effect
finding: Base for Hampton-type work: language models predict human typicality better than vision models. This paper did not test combinations.
numbers: Many LLM and vision models on newer human typicality data across many categories; combined language plus vision predictions beat either alone. Exact correlations not extracted.
limits: Single concepts only. Do not cite as combination evidence.
agent_relevance: Gap: in the sources I opened, nobody measured conjunction overextension or selective modification in modern LLMs.

source: Suresh et al. (2023) Conceptual structure coheres in human cognition but not in large language models
finding: Concept structure estimated from the same LLM varies more across tasks than in humans.
numbers: Abstract and introduction read only: LLM structures individually fairly consistent with human ones but cohere less across tasks than human estimates do. No noun-noun test.
limits: Not a combination study.
agent_relevance: Ask for the same combination in two task formats and use disagreement as a signal.

source: Nagar, Rawal, Dhanania & Tan (2025) How do transformer embeddings represent compositions?
finding: Embedding of a compound is well predicted by composing its parts linearly in modern embedding models; BERT is much worse. Simple addition is nearly as good as ridge regression.
numbers: Cosine with true compound embedding: Google embeddings simple addition 0.852, weighted addition 0.854, ridge 0.922; Mistral addition 0.854, ridge 0.914. Multiplication fails (-0.038). BERT lowest.
limits: Embedding models, not generative reasoning; synthetic adjective-noun data used to visualise.
agent_relevance: If compounds sit near the vector sum of parts, embedding distance between a seed pair and a proposed blend is a cheap code-side coherence or novelty check.

source: Miletic, Schmid & Schulte im Walde (2025) Probing BERT for German compound semantics
finding: Compositionality ratings of 868 German compounds are recoverable from early BERT layers, but best results lag English.
numbers: Constituent-compound cosine correlations with ratings in the range about 0.33-0.43 in some settings and -0.16 to -0.23 in the weakest; earlier-work reference 0.49 (modifier) / 0.59 (head).
limits: German closed compounds; encoder model; numbers read from layout-extracted text.
agent_relevance: Compositionality scores from embeddings are noisy; do not use them alone as gates.

source: Kumar, Ghosh, Tyagi & Manocha (2024) Do vision-language models understand compound nouns? (Compun)
finding: CLIP-style models are weak on compound nouns whose look differs from both parts. Prompting with LLM-written captions that contain the compound fixes part of it.
numbers: 400 compound nouns; text-to-image retrieval among 3: human 96.25%, random 33.33%, CLIP 78.25%, OpenCLIP 83.90%, MetaCLIP 81.35%. With LLM-generated example captions: CLIP 86.50% (+8.25), OpenCLIP 86.25% (+2.35). Reversing the nouns drops CLIP by 37.25 points.
limits: Image retrieval, not language generation; human number from MTurk.
agent_relevance: An LLM-written context sentence measurably improved concept binding. Generated scene context is a useful scaffold.

source: Pan, Chen, He & Zhu (2025) Food image generation on multi-noun categories
finding: Text-to-image models render 'egg noodle' as separate eggs and noodles: each noun is treated as its own object instead of being fused.
numbers: Qualitative failure shown on Stable Diffusion v1-4; fix (FoCULR) adds domain adaptation and core-concept-first layout. Accuracy figures not extracted.
limits: Food domain only.
agent_relevance: Same failure as banana table: parts listed, not fused. Check for fusion, not co-occurrence.

source: Ali et al. (2026) Testing associative creativity in humans and multimodal LLMs with difficult-to-name visual stimuli
finding: Humans give more diverse associative names (e.g. crab spaceship) than multimodal LLMs, with greater semantic distance and entropy; effectiveness declines as stimuli get harder.
numbers: Two datasets (SilCC, PixCC); 60 participants, 120 images in the human set; models include Qwen3-VL-235B and Qwen2.5-VL-72B. Effect sizes not extracted.
limits: Image naming in German; association, not noun-noun definition.
agent_relevance: Opposite direction to KOMBINE: on open naming humans are more diverse, models more valid.

source: Hampton (1987, 1988) Inheritance of attributes in conceptual conjunctions; overextension of conjunctive concepts
finding: Founding human work: a conjunction (pet fish) has emergent attributes not true of either part, and typicality in the conjunction can exceed that in a part. Not read this session.
numbers: not extracted this session
limits: From memory only; verify before use.
agent_relevance: No LLM test of conjunction overextension found; a ready experiment.

source: Wisniewski (1997) When concepts combine
finding: Human noun-noun interpretations split into relation linking, property mapping and hybrids; similar nouns favour property mapping. Not read this session.
numbers: not extracted this session
limits: From memory only; verify.
agent_relevance: The three types are a natural output taxonomy for the agent's blend step.

source: Costello & Keane (2000) Efficient creativity: constraint-guided conceptual combination (C3)
finding: Older AI system that builds noun-noun interpretations under diagnosticity, plausibility and informativeness constraints, tested against human data. Not read this session.
numbers: not extracted this session
limits: From memory only; verify.
agent_relevance: The three constraints are rule-checkable and map to code-side filters.

source: Levin et al. (2019) systematicity in novel noun-compound interpretation (second-hand via Li et al. 2022)
finding: Cited in Li et al.: compound meaning is predictable from whether modifier and head are artifacts or natural kinds. Original not opened.
numbers: Second-hand from Li et al. Table 5: artifact modifier + artifact head 93% event-type meta-relation (N=195); natural-kind modifier + natural-kind head 15% (N=148).
limits: Table read from layout text; original paper unread.
agent_relevance: Relation choice by noun type can be coded as a rule.
